notes:
Summary: Veridian Vault (payment orchestration & fraud analytics) evaluating Redwood Private VPC POC. Strong constraints: keys must remain under customer control (HSM-backed CMKs), audit logs shipped into customer S3 with 7-year retention, and all processing must remain in us-east-1. Customer quote: "We cannot have any key material leave our KMS boundary."

POC objective: prove full Private VPC deployment in customer's AWS account using Terraform + Helm, run representative workloads (chat support agent + embeddings-based fraud lookup), validate KMS integration and audit log delivery, run integration tests and hand over runbook for sign-off.

POC timeline (high-level):
- 2026-02-20: kickoff (Fireflies ff_2026-02-20_1123) – infra requirements agreed, initial network flow diagram exchanged.
- 2026-02-24: customer prepares sandbox AWS account (VPC + subnets + KMS CMK).
- 2026-02-27: Redwood provided Terraform module + Helm chart; SE paired with customer infra for initial apply.
- 2026-03-03: First full deploy in sandbox; basic smoke tests green (see Fireflies ff_2026-03-03_0915).
- 2026-03-05: Integration test run (embedding index build + chat flow); one regression around egress rules.
- 2026-03-10: Security team requested additional audit fields; engineering to patch logging agent.
- 2026-03-12: Planned security walkthrough and sign-off criteria review.

POC implementation notes / technical details:
- Deployment model: Redwood Private control plane disabled for POC; control plane components packaged as Helm chart and installed in customer EKS cluster inside their VPC.
- IaC: Terraform modules provided to create IRSA, KMS key alias binding, S3 bucket with enforced encryption and bucket policy for audit logs.
- KMS integration: Verified CMK rotation policy acceptable; customer requires HSM-backed CMK and restricts CreateGrant/Decrypt to specific IAM principals. Redwood SE documented required IAM/IRSA roles.
- Audit logging: Fluent-bit -> customer S3 + CloudWatch logs; logs must contain token-level request ids, model version, route, and truncated prompt hash. Retention policy 7y.
- Network: need outbound access to Redwood-managed model artifact registry for initial model pulls OR coordinate for pre-seeded AMIs to avoid egress. Customer prefers pre-seeded, but asked for fallback plan.
- Model routing/fallback: requested automatic fallback to Redwood Dedicated in the same region for overload scenarios; billing/legal for fallback still under discussion.

Success criteria for POC (customer sign-off):
1) End-to-end deploy via Terraform/Helm completes in customer sandbox VPC without elevated support.
2) KMS flows work end-to-end: Redwood components can call Encrypt/Decrypt through configured grants and cannot export key material.
3) Audit logs delivered and parsable; sample retention demo provided.
4) Integration tests: chat latency meets target for demo (p95 < 350ms for short-turn chats) and embeddings indexing throughput meets 100 reqs/s baseline.
5) Runbook and automation for repeatable deploy handed to Veridian infra team.

Open questions & next actions:
- Legal to confirm exact phrasing for data residency clause by 2026-03-15.
- SE to provide Terraform plan with mock secrets for Veridian review (ETA 2026-03-11).
- Engineering to add token-level redaction option in audit logs (work item INF-5042).

Customer sentiment / notes from calls:
- CTO: "We want a drop-in private model runtime, but keys cannot be room-for-negotiation."
- Security lead: favors pre-seeded AMIs to avoid egress; will validate with pen-test team.

Stubs / artifacts referenced: pricing-deck (drive), security-FAQ (drive link above), Jira: INF-4987 (network egress), INF-5042 (logging PII redaction).

Short next-step (AE): confirm schedule for 2026-03-12 security walkthrough and deliver Terraform plan by 2026-03-11.
